problem: Find the fundamental vector product of the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨u,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩.$
worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,-v\operatorname{sin}⁡u⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u\operatorname{sin}⁡v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v\operatorname{cos}⁡u)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡v & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ u\operatorname{cos}⁡v & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & -v\operatorname{sin}⁡u \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡u\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & \operatorname{sin}⁡v \\ 0 & u\operatorname{cos}⁡v\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v+uv\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡u,\,u\operatorname{cos}⁡v⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
